reviewer.method: Personally read all 2033 publisher-text lines, five entire original main figures, four one-page supplementary figures and six one-page supplementary tables (all text/cells/pixels). Compared every assigned packet item and patient/family/phase/causal context. Held sources/renderings inherited; byte hashes and PDF extents reverified. No wet-lab work and no benchmark-outcome inspection.

audit.exposure_note: The mandatory HANDOFF.md read at session start exposed aggregate benchmark results and a historical HG002/FGFR2 public-control case-specific rank. No target-case outcome files, current assigned-cohort per-case ranks or evaluator outputs were consulted. This review is not blinded. Prior records retain their original attribution; this reviewer claims only the work specified in method.

limitations: Every assigned mapping (one), allele (one), phenotype (one), sex/age context, negative-feature absence and candidate alternative assessed. This is post-inference source support, not clinical validation.

patient_identity.statement: The family-level packet subject PK-INF-602, female, maps to the sole affected woman IV-4. She married at 20 and had primary infertility over eight years; exact age at examination is not given.
limitations: The packet uses the family identifier rather than IV-4; Table SIII reports male relatives only.

genotype.statement: IV-4 is homozygous for MEIOB c.683-1G>A; the pedigree and chromatogram label her MT/MT. The article reports chr16:1853135C>T from a GRCh37/hg19 pipeline.

evidence.locator: Right pedigree/chromatograms IV-4; main lines 335–336 and 511–524.

limitations: Packet NC_000016.10/hg38 coordinate representation has not been independently remapped or sequence-verified; the shared numeric position alone is insufficient.

segregation.statement: Both parents are WT/MT, the fertile sister IV-3 WT/MT, and affected IV-4, IV-5 and IV-6 MT/MT, as shown by family Sanger sequencing.

evidence.locator: Panel A right-hand PK-INF-602 pedigree and all six chromatograms.

phase.statement: One homozygous splice allele is reported; a two-distinct-variant cis/trans assignment is inapplicable. Parental heterozygosity supports recessive inheritance.

evidence.locator: Panel A PK-INF-602 parental and offspring genotypes.

limitations: No independent long-read, copy-number or sample-level phase assay performed here; this is a source-correspondence assessment.

causal_confidence.statement: MEIOB-associated familial infertility is supported by segregation, abnormal splicing in male relative IV-5, minigene evidence and a mouse model with exon-9 loss and infertility. The packet disease label premature ovarian failure is not clinically established in IV-4: her cycles were regular and the ovarian histology was obtained from mice.

evidence.locator: Lines 511–524, 548–564, 644–658 and 839–853; Figures 1D, 3D; Supplementary Table SV.

limitations: Female-specific hormonal/ovarian-reserve data and human gonadal tissue are unavailable. The mouse allele is a nine-base deletion/one-base insertion producing analogous exon skipping, not the identical human nucleotide substitution. Table SV also retains SSTR5 c.350C>T/p.T117M; it was deprioritized using biological plausibility, not experimentally excluded in the woman. No independent ACMG classification is asserted.

phenotype_completeness.statement: The single positive feature captures the infertility report but omits regular menstrual cycles and the distinction between the woman and her azoospermic brothers. No negative HPO features are encoded. Sex and family matching support IV-4; female hormone values and ovarian histology are not reported.

evidence.locator: Lines 511–524 and 644–658; Supplementary Table SIII (only male patients).

limitations: Normal male hormone values, absent sperm and mouse ovarian follicle loss must not be transferred into the woman’s phenotype. The disease label is more specific than this source establishes.

assessment.statement: The MEIOB symbol, homozygous c.683-1G>A and reference transcript NM_001163560.3 correspond to the reported allele. Exon 9 skipping is experimentally shown in male relative IV-5; p.? retains uncertainty rather than asserting an exact protein HGVS.
limitations: The packet genomic accession and hg38 assembly remain unverified against the paper GRCh37 mapping. No female-specific RNA was analyzed.

assessment.statement: Female infertility is directly described for IV-4, recognized after marriage at age 20 and persisting for eight years; young-adult onset is a reasonable clinical abstraction.
limitations: Time of recognition after marriage does not establish the biological onset. This does not demonstrate premature ovarian failure.
Main text, five figures and all ten supplementary files were personally read/inspected in this resumed session. Prior retrieval/rendering work is inherited and not claimed as newly performed.
Complete component reading does not remove the female ovarian-failure or genomic-build qualifications.
